label: SYNTHETIC READER: a test instrument, never a reader. Fictional; not evidence about the book; not readership.
first_thing_i_would_do: Write the one-page rules file for my own agent with a stop line, then write down who may pull and lift a shared hold before the team touches anything.
why: The hold and the lock story give me a takeaway I can copy with agents I already use, and the shared brief, board and hold is exactly my team's question. But the shared-team part is admitted to be a plan that has not run, so I would want the longer edition to show it running before I paid. The series page tells me nothing I can use.

by_section.why: Clear: a lock that was somebody else's job, asked for, and not done in time. The fair-to-the-conductor turn is the lesson in one line. The figure is described only for the designer, so I take it on trust.
by_section.quote: when one lane is busy, the job waits.

by_section.why: The mechanism is plain: one file, everyone stops, only one person restarts. That is the control my team lacks.
by_section.quote: Anyone on the team could stop everything. Only I could start it again.

by_section.why: Three accounts from different days with no ruling is honest, but on a phone between meetings I wanted the takeaway first. The last account (token usage) adds almost nothing after the first.
by_section.quote: I am not going to pick one for you now.

by_section.section: What did not work: the interview
by_section.why: The freeze lesson is the most practical thing in the chapter. Deck and the storyteller blur into each other as two rueful agents that ran out of time.
by_section.quote: when you freeze something, write down what is waiting to go in when you unfreeze it.

by_section.section: After the hold: the empty chair
by_section.why: Short and abstract. I do not know what the independent member would have done, so the advice to staff it first has no concrete form for me.
by_section.quote: a second reading, not a second identity.

by_section.why: Direct and doable in ten minutes, and it names the restart question.
by_section.quote: Until you have, nobody restarts it.

by_section.why: Short and useful: the agents are temporary, the written record is what carries over.
by_section.quote: The team is temporary. The record is not.

by_section.why: Eight job descriptions in a row is a roster, and I could not tell which I would need. It reads as an introduction to a cast rather than a pattern to copy.
by_section.quote: Every number in this book is in my register, or it is not in this book.

by_section.section: Two scenes from the second factory
by_section.why: A refused line and a rule that failed on the night, both kept in. This is what makes me trust the rest.
by_section.quote: The rule was right. I was a wake too late to use it.

by_section.why: This is my situation: several people, each with their own agents. One brief owner, a board read each morning, a hold anyone can pull. It is labelled a plan, which I respect, though I would push back on one owner for the brief if that person is away.
by_section.quote: Two people editing one brief is how a team ends up with two briefs.

by_section.why: The five steps with a check under each are the nearest thing to a recipe. The shop owner example makes the rules file real. I stall on tool choice: it says 'an AI agent tool' and names none, and gives no sense of how long step 1 to 4 takes.
by_section.quote: If you cannot say when it must stop, it does not have one.

by_section.why: One line I can act on.
by_section.quote: Ship something somebody else can use, then do it again.

by_section.section: A book about you doing it
by_section.why: A series blurb with no takeaway for my team. Generation labels and 'Faro' mean nothing to me, and it arrives after the one useful page.
by_section.quote: Generation ZX is not a range of birth years

best_line: Anyone on the team could stop everything. Only I could start it again.
worst_moment: Chapter 6, the series page: it is a brand statement after a practical chapter, with no step to take. Second worst, the roster of eight in chapter 5 'The second factory', which names jobs but not which one a small team should add second.
cut: Chapter 6 entirely, or reduce it to a single line linking to the series; trim the third answer in 'Why stop then'; shorten the roster in chapter 5 to the three or four roles a first team needs.
notes: Missing for a conference team: which tool to start with, how long the first day takes, how the shared board is actually kept (a file, a tracker, a chat?), and what happens to the hold when the person who may lift it is in a talk or on a plane. The 'one central person' risk is partly answered by the named deputy for lifting the hold, but the brief still has a single owner. Figures and maps are described for the designer only, so I judged the text alone.
